import pandas as pd

# File paths for source CSVs
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_17/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_17/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_17/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_17/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_17/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_17/training_5.csv",
]

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    # index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column as per instructions
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# Concatenate all source DataFrames (UNION operation)
df_all = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The schema matches target schema exactly, but we need to ensure types and formatting:
# Target Schema:
# ['S/N': int, 'Building/Project Name': str, 'Street Name': str, 'Postal District': int,
#  'Type': str, 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)': str, 'Monthly Gross Rent($)': int,
#  'Floor Area (sq ft)': str, 'Lease Commencement Date': str]

# Fix data types and clean data:

# 1. 'S/N' should be integer
df_all['S/N'] = pd.to_numeric(df_all['S/N'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# 2. 'Building/Project Name' as string, strip whitespace
df_all['Building/Project Name'] = df_all['Building/Project Name'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 3. 'Street Name' as string, strip whitespace
df_all['Street Name'] = df_all['Street Name'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 4. 'Postal District' as integer
df_all['Postal District'] = pd.to_numeric(df_all['Postal District'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# 5. 'Type' as string, strip whitespace
df_all['Type'] = df_all['Type'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 6. 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)' as string
# In source 2, there is a value 'na*' which should be normalized to 'na' or empty string
df_all['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'] = df_all['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'].astype(str).str.strip()
df_all['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'] = df_all['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'].replace({'na*': 'na', 'nan': 'na'})

# 7. 'Monthly Gross Rent($)' as integer
df_all['Monthly Gross Rent($)'] = pd.to_numeric(df_all['Monthly Gross Rent($)'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# 8. 'Floor Area (sq ft)' as string, strip whitespace
df_all['Floor Area (sq ft)'] = df_all['Floor Area (sq ft)'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 9. 'Lease Commencement Date' as string, strip whitespace
df_all['Lease Commencement Date'] = df_all['Lease Commencement Date'].astype(str).str.strip()

# Final target DataFrame
Target5_17 = df_all[
    ['S/N', 'Building/Project Name', 'Street Name', 'Postal District', 'Type',
     'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)', 'Monthly Gross Rent($)', 'Floor Area (sq ft)', 'Lease Commencement Date']
]

# Write to target CSV file without index
Target5_17.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_0.csv', index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_1.csv', index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_2.csv', index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_3.csv', index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_4.csv', index_col=0)
df5 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/training_5.csv', index_col=0)

# Union all source tables (concatenate)
df = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2, df3, df4, df5], ignore_index=True)

# Convert 'Monthly Gross Rent($)' to numeric (int), coercing errors to NaN, then fill NaN with 0 for aggregation
df['Monthly Gross Rent($)'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Monthly Gross Rent($)'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Group by all leftmost non-float columns except the aggregation column
# According to target schema and hints:
# Group by: ['S/N', 'Building/Project Name', 'Street Name', 'Postal District', 'Type', 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)', 'Floor Area (sq ft)', 'Lease Commencement Date']
# Aggregate sum on 'Monthly Gross Rent($)'
group_cols = ['S/N', 'Building/Project Name', 'Street Name', 'Postal District', 'Type', 
              'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)', 'Floor Area (sq ft)', 'Lease Commencement Date']

df_grouped = df.groupby(group_cols, dropna=False, as_index=False).agg({'Monthly Gross Rent($)': 'sum'})

# Ensure column order matches target schema exactly
df_grouped = df_grouped[['S/N', 'Building/Project Name', 'Street Name', 'Postal District', 'Type', 
                         'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)', 'Monthly Gross Rent($)', 'Floor Area (sq ft)', 
                         'Lease Commencement Date']]

# Convert 'Postal District' to int (target type)
df_grouped['Postal District'] = pd.to_numeric(df_grouped['Postal District'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Convert 'S/N' to int (target type)
df_grouped['S/N'] = pd.to_numeric(df_grouped['S/N'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Write to target CSV file
df_grouped.to_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_17/target_multisource_critique_history.csv', index=False)
